brief: Tonight is Pull B, and it is the first one since 3 September — twelve days, and the only Pull B you have done at this gym. Here is the thing that shaped the whole card. Looking at the clock stamps on that 3 September session, the bent-over row, the close-grip pulldown and the first straight-arm set were all typed in within about twenty seconds of each other, right at the start. Those lifts happened before you opened the app and the numbers were filled in from memory afterwards. That is not a complaint — it is just that half of tonight's reference numbers are things you remembered, not things anyone measured. So the card splits in two. Where 3 September was logged live, set by set with real rests, you go up. Where it was typed in from memory, you repeat the exact same number and we get one honest reading first. Going up: the shrugs to 85 for twelve, because 80 for fifteen three times was clean live work at the top of the range. The incline curls to 27.5 for nine and eight, same reason — ten and ten at 25 was the full ask, logged properly. Holding at last time's numbers: the close-grip pulldown stays at 77, 83 and 88 for ten. The app wanted to add weight to all three. Those numbers were entered in six seconds and four days ago your wide-grip pulldown actually slid back from 93 to 88 and lost a rep, so 88 is already the edge on that stack. Do it live tonight and it moves next time. The straight-arm pulldown is three sets at 46. Your own note from that night says the first set was a machine and the other two were the cable crossover, so that one slot is currently two different pieces of equipment sharing a name. Three sets on the cable at 46 makes the number mean one thing. The reverse curls stay at 37.5 for eleven, eleven and ten. The app has been printing twelve reps there and you got ten, eleven, ten — beat eleven twice and the weight goes up. Face pulls stay at 27.5. On 3 September you got fifteen and fifteen; on 10 September, same weight, both sets came in at thirteen. The more recent night is the one that counts, so no extra weight. Now the row, and you should know this was the argument of the night. Your recovery trainer wanted it taken off the card completely — tonight is your third training day in a row, the numbers are remembered rather than measured, and the slot still says Smith Bent-Over Row at a gym that has no Smith machine, so nobody here knows what you actually rowed on. I overruled that and the row stays, at exactly the weights you reported last time: 120 and 140 for nine, then 150 and 155 for eight. It adds nothing — it is the same load you said you did. Skipping it would leave your main back lift untouched for another twelve days and we would still not know what the number means. Doing it tonight settles it. Two things I want from you on that lift: write down what you actually row on in this building, and stop any set the moment your back rounds. If 155 turns out to be a weight you never really did, coming up short is the information — log what happened. Last, two things that are not about tonight. You have not logged your bodyweight since 23 August, which is twenty-three days, and the show is 1 March — that is the single most useful number you are not giving us. And the last cardio you logged was 21 July. The deload starts on 21 September, six days out, which is a good window to put some easy conditioning back in without it costing you anything in the gym.

Two more slots name a Smith machine you do not have: the incline press on Push A and the RDL on Legs B. There is no barbell row, no chest-supported row and no non-Smith RDL in the exercise list, so no Yes/No card can fix these three. This one needs you and me in a session, not a tap at the gym.
This is your third training day in a row, after a 40-minute Legs A and a 68-minute Push B. Nothing tonight adds a set, and only two lifts add weight.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August — twenty-three days — and the show is 1 March. Step on a scale this week; your recovery trainer says it cannot read you properly without it.
Meso 2, week 4 of 4 — the last hard week. The deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, five disagreements settled, one tiredness veto overruled, no pain or injury objection.

proposals.why: Both push days now press dumbbells overhead at 8 to 10 reps, and Push B does it first and heaviest, so this takes the Push A sets to 10 to 12 and lets the two days stop being the same session — the same way your chest press already splits 10 to 12 on Push A and 8 to 10 on Push B.

overrides.reason: Exactly the weights you reported on 3 September — this adds nothing. Your recovery trainer wanted this lift off the card tonight because those numbers were typed in from memory and this is your third day running; I kept it because skipping leaves your main back lift unread for another twelve days. Write down what you actually row on here, and stop any set when your back rounds. Coming up short is information.

Same as last time on purpose. All three of these sets were entered within six seconds on 3 September, so they are remembered numbers, and four days ago your wide-grip pulldown fell back from 93 to 88 and lost a rep. Log these live tonight and the weight moves next Pull B.

Your note says the first set was a machine and the other two were the cable crossover, so this one slot is two different machines sharing a name. All three sets on the cable at 46 — the only part of that night that was logged live — so the number finally means one thing.

This was logged properly, set by set with real rests, and you finished fifteen on all three sets at 80 — the top of the range. The dumbbells go up to 85 and the rep target resets to twelve. If this rack has no 85s, take the next pair up and log what you used.

Ten reps on both sets at 25, live-logged with real rests, is the full ask for this slot — so the 27.5s are earned. If this rack jumps straight from 25 to 30, take the 30s and get eight; that is still inside the range.

The app has this one flagged as stuck and keeps printing twelve reps; you did ten, eleven and ten at 37.5. The weight holds and the card now asks for what is actually in front of you. Beat eleven on the first two sets and the next step is yours.

Fifteen and fifteen at 27.5 on 3 September, but a week later at the same weight both sets came in at thirteen. The more recent night counts, so no extra weight tonight. Clear both sets again and it moves.

dissent.progression: Hold at last time's exact weights — 120 and 140 for nine, 150 and 155 for eight — since every set stopped at eight, the bottom of the range.
dissent.recovery: Take it off the card entirely: third training day in a row, the numbers were typed in from memory, and nobody knows what he rowed on at a gym with no Smith machine.
dissent.why: Recovery is right about every fact and I still kept the lift. Its veto was on tiredness, not pain, so I was allowed to weigh it. What decided me is that progression's call adds nothing — it is the same load he told us he did — and that skipping is the one option that guarantees we still do not know what this slot means in twelve days' time. The unknown here is the implement and the provenance, and the only thing that resolves either is him doing the lift and logging it live. The deload is six days out, so fatigue banked tonight gets wiped. I have put both of recovery's concerns on the card itself: write down what you row on, and stop the set when form goes.

dissent.progression: Add five pounds to all three sets — 82, 88, 93 — because he hit ten reps on all three at 77, 83 and 88.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 77, 83 and 88 exactly; those three sets were entered inside six seconds, so they are recalled numbers and nothing should be built on top of them.
dissent.why: Progression's rule is sound but it is being applied to a number nobody measured. Adding five pounds to a remembered weight compounds a guess instead of testing it. Recovery also brought the one piece of live evidence from this gym's pulldowns: on 10 September the wide-grip went 88, 93, then back to 88 for nine, so 93 is already the edge on that stack. Repeating gives us a real reading tonight and the step is still there next week.

dissent.progression: Open at 46 for twelve, then two sets at 51 — he did 46 for twelve twice on the cable and that is the top of the range.
dissent.recovery: Three sets at 46, all on the cable, because his note shows the slot was a machine for one set and the cable for two and the number has to mean one thing first.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the slot is currently two machines wearing one name, and both want it consolidated onto the cable. They split on whether to add weight while doing it. Recovery's version is already a real increase in work — he goes from one set at 22 plus two at 46 to three full sets at 46 — and changing the implement and the load in the same night would leave us unable to read the result either way. Fix what the slot is tonight, move the weight next time.

dissent.progression: Up to 85 for twelve on all three sets — fifteen reps at 80 on every set is the top of the range.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 80 for fifteen; the lift is fine but this is a third straight training day and not the night to add weight.
dissent.why: This is the cleanest earned raise on the card and recovery said so itself — its words were that there is nothing wrong with the lift. Its objection is about the day, not the shrug, and a shrug is close to the cheapest lift in the program in terms of what it takes out of you. The 80 for fifteen was logged live, set by set, with real rests, so unlike most of that session it is a measured number. Earned on measured data beats a general caution about the calendar.

dissent.progression: Up to 27.5 for nine and eight — ten reps on both sets at 25 is the top of this slot.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 25 for ten and do not chase the missing third set on a third straight training day.
dissent.why: Recovery's reasoning rests on a mistake: it read two sets as a shortfall, but this slot was cut to two sets on 2 September and he accepted that, so two sets at 25 for ten was the complete ask, finished. Correcting that removes the whole basis for holding. The sets were live-logged with real rests, the reps were at the top of the range, and a two-set curl at the end of the night costs almost nothing.
